kicker: ONE REPORT FOR THE COWORK VALUE STORY
title: Cowork Value Intelligence
subtitle: Adoption, delegated work, workflow maturity, and transparent value—connected in one report.
text: Meet Cowork Value Intelligence: one Power BI report that turns Cowork activity into a clear story about adoption, the work people delegate, how deeply they delegate it, and the value those workflows may create. The template is data-free by design and comes to life with your approved organization exports. Here is a quick tour of the decisions it supports.

title: Start Here
subtitle: One report, six questions, and a clear evidence path
caption: Begin with the decision, then follow the right evidence.
text: Start Here is home base. It routes leaders to the questions that matter: Is adoption growing? Who is using Cowork? What work is being delegated? Where is value concentrating? Which workflows need enablement? What should happen next? The report begins with the decision and guides you to the right evidence.

title: Activity & Value
subtitle: Skills, work categories, and departmental momentum
caption: Target enablement where real workflows are already taking hold.
text: Activity and Value shows where Cowork is becoming part of everyday work: which skills are used most, which categories contribute the most estimated hours, and which departments are building momentum. This turns generic training into targeted workflow enablement.

title: Actions
subtitle: Skills, categories, value tiers, and repeatable workflows
caption: The goal is not more prompts—it is better, higher-value work.
text: Actions explains what people ask Cowork to do. Move from skill volume to work categories and value tiers, spot unmapped tools, and identify repeatable actions worth scaling. The goal is not more prompts. It is better, higher-value work.

title: How Far They Delegate
subtitle: Duration, steps, skill chaining, and ladder movement
caption: See where users are ready to move from trying to delegating.
text: How Far They Delegate goes beyond activity. It shows task duration, steps, skill chaining, and movement from trying to using, delegating, and automating. These signals show workflow depth—not unattended work—and where users are ready for advanced patterns.

eyebrow: CHAMPIONS · WHO CAN SCALE THE PATTERN
title: Value by User Tier
subtitle: Concentration, champions, dependencies, and coaching
caption: Pair user tiers with business context before targeting action.
text: Value by User Tier reveals whether adoption is broad or concentrated. Find champions who can teach proven patterns, teams that depend on a few experts, and users who may need coaching. Pair each tier with business context before acting.

title: Transparent Value Methodology
subtitle: Observed activity plus explicit, adjustable assumptions
caption: Scenario planning with assumptions you can see, change, and document.
text: The methodology page keeps the value story defensible. Every output traces to observed task volume, published time-saved assumptions, a selected labor rate, and optional quality adjustments. Change the assumptions and the result changes. This is scenario planning, not audited savings.

title: From usage data to an enablement strategy
bullets: See whether adoption is growing and returning.
Understand which work people delegate—and how deeply.
Identify champions and workflows worth scaling.
Make value assumptions visible and challengeable.
Use consumption as supporting context, not the headline.
footer: Evidence-aware template · Approved customer exports remain the source · Decision support, not official billing
text: Together, these views answer the questions leaders have: Is adoption growing? What work is being delegated? Are people moving into deeper workflows? Where are the champions? Which patterns should we scale next? Consumption and cost are available when needed, but they support the story—they do not define it.
